```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This page lists every setting in harnessr, stage by stage, and the building
blocks those settings choose between. harnessr builds the tables from
`gr_settings_table()` and the registries when the page is built, so they match
the installed code.

A setting with a walkthrough links to it. The walkthrough is a section of a
guide that covers what the setting trades off, the signs that you should
change it, where its default came from and how to test a change.

```{r message = FALSE}
library(harnessr)
old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE, embedder = "lexical")
settings <- gr_settings_table()
table(settings$stage, settings$tier)[unique(settings$stage), ]
```

## Reading the tables

Each row is one setting, and these columns describe it:

- `where`: the function that takes the setting.
- `default`: the value used when you give none. A string appears without
  quotes, a set of choices shows its first choice, and anything else appears
  as R code.
- `tier`: `basic` for the few settings most runs change, `advanced` for the
  rest.
- `status`: where the default came from. `measured` means a measurement backs
  it, `cited` means a published source gives it, and `untested` means it was
  chosen and nothing has measured it. A blank means nothing is declared, as
  for switches, limits and most function arguments.

`gr_settings_table()` also returns the `source` behind each status. For the
full help, see `?gr_read_spec`, `?gr_segment_spec`, `?gr_ingest_spec` and
`?hr_options`.

You give a setting where its stage takes it. Ingest, segment and read
settings go in a spec (`gr_read_spec(top_k = 4)`), in a recipe, or by name to
`answer_document()`, `gr_read_many()` and `gr_arm()`, which put each on the
step it belongs to. Review and evaluation settings are arguments of their
functions. You set options for the session with `hr_options()`.

To find out whether a value works better on your documents, build one arm per
value with `hr_sweep()` and compare the arms with `hr_benchmark()` and
`hr_report()`, as `vignette("compare")` does. `hr_sweep_check()` reports
which values sent the same requests.

```{r}
show_settings <- function(stage) {
  s <- settings[settings$stage == stage, ]
  esc <- function(x) gsub("|", "\\|", ifelse(is.na(x), "", x), fixed = TRUE)
  name <- ifelse(is.na(s$guide), paste0("`", s$name, "`"),
                 sprintf("[`%s`](%s.html#%s)", s$name, sub("#.*", "", s$guide),
                         sub(".*#", "", s$guide)))
  knitr::kable(data.frame(setting = name, where = paste0("`", s$where, "`"),
                          default = paste0("`", esc(s$default), "`"),
                          tier = s$tier, status = esc(s$status),
                          description = esc(s$description)),
               row.names = FALSE)
}
```

## Ingest

These settings control what comes out of a file: cleaning, OCR, the PDF
layout pass, and the floor on how much text must survive. The entries of
`cleaner_opts` and `layout_opts` appear under their parent's name, as
`cleaner_opts.references_after`. `vignette("ingest")` covers them.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("ingest")
```

## Segment

harnessr cuts the text into chunks with these settings. `vignette("segment")`
covers them.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("segment")
```

## Read

These settings decide how the model reads the chunks. The stage also holds
the ones `gr_read_many()` adds for a folder. `vignette("readers")` covers
them.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("read")
```

## Screening

The arguments of these functions, which `vignette("review")` covers:

- `gr_screen()`, which decides which documents a review reads.
- `gr_reference()` and `gr_calibrate()`, which measure the screening against a
  person.
- `gr_screen_sample_size()` and `gr_stop_test()`, the sample size and stopping
  tests.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("screen")
```

## Extraction

The arguments of `gr_extract()`. The recipe settings you pass to it in `...`
are the ingest and segment settings above.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("extract")
```

## Synthesis

The arguments of `gr_claims()`, `gr_outline()`, `gr_gaps()` and
`gr_synthesise()`.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("synthesise")
```

## Evaluation

The arguments of `hr_benchmark()`, `hr_report()`, `hr_judge()` and
`gr_compare()`. `vignette("evaluate")` and `vignette("compare")` cover them.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("evaluate")
```

## Options

Session settings. You set them with `hr_options()`, and a run reads them when
it starts. `vignette("runs")` covers the limits.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("options")
```

## Building blocks

Some settings choose a module from a registry: `extractor`, `clean`, `method`,
`reader`, `hr_options(embedder = )`, and the recipe given to
`answer_document()`. The tables below are the registries as installed, so a
module you register with `gr_register_reader()` and the like
(`vignette("extending")`) appears in them too.

### Extractors

An extractor turns one kind of file into text. It is chosen by the file's
extension unless `extractor` names one.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_extractors()[, c("name", "extensions", "needs", "description")])
```

### Cleaners and presets

A cleaner removes one kind of noise from the text. Those marked `default_on`
run unless the preset or list you give leaves them out; `early` cleaners run
before `late` ones whatever order they are named in.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_cleaners()[, c("name", "stage", "default_on", "description")])
```

A preset is a named list of cleaners. The steps each one runs, read from what
it did to the example report:

```{r}
presets <- c("none", "minimal", "standard", "academic", "scan", "legacy")
knitr::kable(data.frame(preset = presets, cleaners = vapply(presets, function(p) {
  steps <- names(gr_ingest(gr_example(), gr_ingest_spec(clean = p))$stats$clean_log)
  if (length(steps)) paste(steps, collapse = ", ") else "(none)"
}, character(1)), row.names = NULL))
```

### Segmenters

A segmenter decides where chunks are cut. `cost` says what it spends:
`free`, one embedding pass, or model requests.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_segmenters()[, c("name", "cost", "needs_client", "description")])
```

### Readers

A reader decides how the chunks reach the model. `signature` is which chunks
are sent, how many requests, and how information passes between them;
`cost_calls` is the number of requests.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_readers()[, c("name", "signature", "cost_calls", "description")])
```

### Embedders

An embedder turns text into vectors for `retrieve`, `iterative` and the
`semantic` segmenter. A deterministic one gives the same vectors every run,
which a replay needs.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_embedders()[, c("name", "deterministic", "description")])
```

### Recipes

A recipe names an ingestion, a segmentation and a reader with their settings.
These are the values each built-in recipe sets; any of them can be overridden
by name.

```{r}
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(gr_recipes()), function(n) {
  r <- gr_recipes(n)
  data.frame(recipe = n, clean = paste(r$ingest$clean, collapse = ", "),
             method = r$segment$method, max_tokens = r$segment$max_tokens,
             overlap_tokens = r$segment$overlap_tokens, reader = r$read$reader,
             top_k = r$read$top_k)
})))
```

```{r include = FALSE}
hr_options(old)
```
